Hi Claire — great next steps. Recap + recommended approach below so your team can circulate internally. TL;DR: start hosted sandbox for Day 0 validation, run dedicated sandbox for throughput and end-to-end latency, reserve VPC only if you need data plane isolation for the POC.

1) Recommended POC environments (phased)
  - Phase A (fast path, 2–3 days): Redwood Hosted sandbox (no infra onboarding) — best for prompt/quality evaluation and quick checks at scale.
  - Phase B (4–7 days to spin up): Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPUs) — mirrors production throughput and 99th percentile latency; we can set fixed concurrency and sequence lengths to reproduce your worst-case scenarios.
  - Phase C (optional, 7–14 days to onboard): Private VPC — required only if procurement / security requires tenant-isolated network + KMS. Adds onboarding time but matches your future production posture.

2) Success criteria suggestions (proposed, we can update from your sheet)
  - Quality: BLEU/ROUGE-style pass rate on curated clinical prompt set >= 88% agreement with internal grader; no high-severity hallucinations in top-100 prompts.
  - Latency: p50 < 120ms, p95 < 300ms, p99 < 500ms under the POC traffic profile (3 clients, burst windows up to 200 rps).
  - Reliability: <= 1% error rate over 72-hour continuous run, KV cache hit rate > 30% for prefix-heavy workloads.

3) Proposed timeline (start date target Oct 5)
  - Oct 5: Phase A hosted sandbox activated + baseline eval (1–2 days)
  - Oct 8: Phase B dedicated pool requested, capacity reserved (provisioning 2–3 business days)
  - Oct 12–15: 72-hour soak test and throughput-limited runs
  - Oct 16: POC readout and decision to proceed to VPC/prod path (if needed)

4) Owners / day-to-day ops (Redwood)
  - Onboarding lead: Lukas Meyer — primary contact for env config, prompt telemetry, and success criteria instrumentation.
  - Performance lead: Ben Carter — will own dedicated pool sizing, batching settings, and latency tuning.
  - Customer success: Laura Bennett — responsible for onboarding checklist, access, and regular standups.

5) Quick asks from Mediq to speed activation
  - Finalized clinical prompt set (CSV) and traffic profile (burst RPS; payload sizes)
  - Security contact for RFI/SOC2 exchange (if procurement is involved)
  - PO or signed MOU for reserved capacity if you want Phase B guaranteed throughput

Next steps: I can provision the hosted sandbox this week and send credentials; Ben will follow up with a dedicated sizing note tomorrow. If that sounds good, confirm the Oct 5 kick.

Thanks,
Lukas
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick sizing and cost guidance to help procurement:

- Phase A (hosted sandbox): minimal cost, metered; sufficient for prompt quality checks and small-scale latency numbers but not for sustained high-concurrency tests.
- Phase B (dedicated sandbox): recommend 2xA100-equivalent nodes for the 200rps burst profile — estimated reserved cost: ~$12k/week (includes monitoring + support). We can reduce cost by enabling quantized model variants for non-critical prompts.
- Phase C (VPC): adds ~3–5 business days for network onboarding and KMS integration; infra cost similar to dedicated but with network isolation premium.

I'll attach the MOU template and a rough SOW snippet for procurement review. If procurement needs a tighter cost cap, we can propose a staged reserve (e.g., reserve 1 node and burst above into hosted).
